top_story: Washington is pairing coercive diplomacy with a broader regional realignment: after military strikes, Trump shifted on 20 August toward threatening Iran’s trade partners, building on his 17 August warning that even Oman could be targeted if it obstructs a deal, a posture that raises risks for Gulf states and commercial networks already exposed to conflict spillover. Hours later, Israel’s admission that its soldiers fired on the car in which Hind Rajab and six relatives were killed in Gaza reopened one of the war’s most emblematic civilian cases and underscored how accountability remains reactive, not preventive. The emerging picture is of regional diplomacy advancing through intimidation while impunity and openly exclusionary rhetoric deepen Palestinian vulnerability and narrow the space for any durable settlement.
